Formula theta_i = atan2(dy, dx) of segment i, in [0, 2 pi) (axial: folded into [0, pi)); phi_i = m theta_i with m = 1 (directional) or 2 (axial). C = sum w_i cos(phi_i), S = sum w_i sin(phi_i), W = sum w_i over segments with positive finite length and weight. Mean angle = atan2(S, C) / m, resultant length R = sqrt(C^2 + S^2) / W, circular variance V = 1 - R, Rayleigh z = ((sum cos(phi_i))^2 + (sum sin(phi_i))^2) / n = n Rbar_0^2, using each of the n valid directions once, independently of descriptive weights. Rbar_0 is the unweighted resultant, distinct from the weighted R. This is not giddy Rose permutation inference; no p-value is returned. Bins are left-closed equal-width sectors of the period (2 pi, or pi when axial) holding the summed weight. When no valid segment remains, count and bins are zero and the other summary fields are NaN.

\begin{aligned}
\term{circularAngle}{\phi_i}&=m\,\theta_i,\qquad m=1\ \text{(directional) or } 2\ \text{(axial)}\\
\term{cosineSum}{C}&=\sum_i w_i\cos\phi_i,\qquad \term{sineSum}{S}=\sum_i w_i\sin\phi_i,\qquad \term{totalWeight}{W}=\sum_i w_i\\
\term{resultant}{R}&=\frac{\sqrt{C^2+S^2}}{W},\qquad \term{meanAngle}{\bar{\theta}}=\tfrac{1}{m}\operatorname{atan2}(S,C),\qquad V=1-R\\
\term{rayleighZ}{z}&=\frac{(\sum_i\cos\phi_i)^2+(\sum_i\sin\phi_i)^2}{\term{validCount}{n}}=n\,\bar{R}_0^2
\end{aligned}
